title: Mineral and Energy Resources of India

questions.question: Which iron ore is considered the finest, with up to about 70 percent iron content?
questions.rationale: Magnetite is the highest-grade ore with up to about 70 percent iron; haematite carries 50-60 percent and is the most widely used.

questions.question: High-grade haematite from the Bailadila hills is exported through which port?
questions.rationale: Ore from the Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt is railed from Bailadila in Chhattisgarh to Visakhapatnam for export.

questions.question: Manganese is mined mainly because it:
questions.rationale: Manganese is a ferro-alloy used to harden and strengthen steel, so it travels with iron ore to the steel industry.

questions.question: Aluminium is smelted from which ore?
questions.rationale: Bauxite is the ore of aluminium; smelters such as NALCO's at Koraput sit near bauxite deposits and cheap electricity.

questions.question: The Koderma belt of Jharkhand is famous for which mineral used in electrical insulation?
questions.rationale: The Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh belt of Jharkhand, with Nellore in Andhra Pradesh, supplies most of India's mica.

questions.question: Jharia in Jharkhand is celebrated in India's coal geography for:
options: The richest coking coal of the Gondwana belt
questions.rationale: Jharia holds India's richest coking (metallurgical) coal within the Gondwana rocks of the Damodar valley.

questions.question: Which is India's oldest petroleum refinery, working since 1901?
questions.rationale: Digboi in eastern Assam refined crude from India's oldest oil field and remains the country's oldest working refinery.

questions.question: India's vast thorium reserves, important for its nuclear programme, come from:
options: Monazite sands of the Kerala coast
questions.rationale: Monazite beach sands along the Kerala coast are rich in thorium, a long-term nuclear fuel for advanced reactors.

questions.question: Bhadla, one of the world's largest solar parks, is located in which state?
questions.rationale: Bhadla lies in the sun-drenched Thar desert of Rajasthan, a flagship site of the National Solar Mission.

questions.question: Why is recycling aluminium scrap counted as energy conservation?
options: It uses far less energy than smelting new metal
It eliminates the need for power plants
questions.rationale: Recycling aluminium consumes only a small fraction of the electricity needed to smelt fresh metal from bauxite.
